Title: GET /ping returns HTTP 201 Created instead of 200 OK
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Open Postman. 2. Create GET request to https://restful-booker.herokuapp.com/ping. 3. Send request. 4. Observe HTTP status code.
Comments: Health-check endpoints conventionally return 200; 201 implies a resource was created

Title: DELETE /booking/:id returns HTTP 201 Created instead of 204 No Content
Preconditions: Valid auth token and existing booking id
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Authenticate via POST /auth to obtain a token. 2. Create a booking via POST /booking and note its bookingid. 3. Send DELETE /booking/<id> with header Cookie: token=<token>. 4. Observe status code.
Expected Result: HTTP 204 No Content with empty body
Comments: RFC 7231 recommends 204 for a successful DELETE with no payload

Title: POST /booking accepts invalid date strings in bookingdates
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send POST /booking with JSON body where bookingdates.checkin = "invalid-date" and bookingdates.checkout = "not-a-date". 2. Observe response.
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with validation message
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK - booking created with invalid dates stored
Comments: Dates should be validated against ISO-8601 (YYYY-MM-DD)

Title: POST /booking accepts negative totalprice
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send POST /booking with totalprice = -100. 2. Observe response.
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request - negative price is not a valid amount
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK - booking created with totalprice -100

Title: POST /booking accepts checkout date earlier than checkin date
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send POST /booking with bookingdates.checkin = "2026-12-31" and bookingdates.checkout = "2026-01-01". 2. Observe response.
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request - checkout must be after checkin
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK - booking created with reversed date range
Comments: Logical validation missing; causes negative-length stays

Title: PUT and PATCH on non-existent booking id return 405 instead of 404
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Authenticate via POST /auth. 2. Send PUT (or PATCH) /booking/99999999 with valid auth header and a valid payload. 3. Observe status code.
Expected Result: HTTP 404 Not Found - resource does not exist
Comments: 404 is more accurate; 405 implies the method is not supported at all

Title: POST /booking with missing required field returns 500 Internal Server Error
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send POST /booking with one of firstname/lastname/totalprice/depositpaid/bookingdates omitted. 2. Observe status code and response body.
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request with a descriptive validation error
Comments: Any invalid client input should map to 4xx
column14: never 5xx. Sensitive implementation details may leak

Title: POST /auth has no rate-limiting / brute-force protection
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send 100+ POST /auth requests with wrong credentials within seconds using a script or Postman Collection Runner. 2. Observe responses - all return normally with no throttling.
Actual Result: response should be 429 Too Many Requests or account locked
Status: All 100+ attempts return 200 with reason "Bad credentials" and no throttling
column14: Security risk - passwords can be brute-forced without detection

Title: POST /booking does not enforce a maximum length on firstname/lastname
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send POST /booking with firstname containing 10000 characters. 2. Observe response.
Expected Result: HTTP 400 Bad Request - field length exceeded
Actual Result: HTTP 200 OK - booking created with 10k-char firstname

Title: POST /auth returns HTTP 200 on failed authentication instead of 401 Unauthorized
Steps to Reproduce: 1. Send POST /auth with wrong credentials. 2. Observe status code.
Comments: RESTful convention - authentication failures should return 401
